Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

I'm so excited to be bringing this workshop for the third time to Nelson this Sept 2026.

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Sunday 20th September - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm


Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Overview

A safe, friendly and relaxed space to arrive as you are while connecting with other amazing people .

Life feels a little better in good company!

We’d love to invite you to join us for an evening of genuine conversation, laughter, thoughtful moments, and meaningful connection in a warm and welcoming space.

The idea behind Good Company

We believe, there is something special about sitting down with good people, sharing stories, listening with curiosity, and leaving feeling a little more connected than when you walked in.

This isn't about having the right answers or trying to fix one another. It's about slowing down, being ourselves, sharing different perspectives, reflecting together, and simply enjoying being in good company.

Each gathering explores a different aspect of everyday life through thoughtful conversation, offering a chance to hear how the same topic can resonate differently with each person in the room.




The topic for this evening is:

"What makes you feel alive?"




What to expect

We'll welcome you with a hot cup of tea or coffee and some light snacks before settling in together.

The evening will be gently guided with a few conversation prompts, while leaving plenty of space for the conversation to unfold naturally. There isn't a speaker and there isn't an audience.

The conversation belongs to all of us, and every person who joins helps shape the evening.

As a special touch, we encourage you to bring something that connects with the theme. It could be an object, a photograph, a favourite book, a poem, a piece of music, art or anything else that holds meaning for you. You're welcome to share the story behind it, or simply keep it with you during the evening.

If this feels like your kind of evening, we'd love to welcome you.

To keep the gathering personal and conversational, places are limited to 10 participants.




A couple of notes

• Good Company is a safe, respectful, inclusive and kind space for everyone. We value open conversation, thoughtful listening, different perspectives, and treating one another with care.

• This isn't a place for political, ideological or religious advocacy or debate.

• It is not intended to be a clinical therapy or crisis support group.

• Please let us know in advance if you have any accessibility requirements or dietary needs, and we'll do our best to accommodate you.

• Tickets are offered as a Flexible Contribution to help cover the basic costs of the gathering. If cost would prevent you from joining us, please get in touch.

• Please arrive at 3:45PM for 4:00PM start

• The venue is located on the first floor inside the arcade. Please walk towards the stairs near the lift at the end of the arcade, Astanga Yoga studio will be on your right hand side.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Special General Meeting

At the Special General Meeting, whānau will be asked to consider proposed amendments to the Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō Trust Deed and the Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō Charitable Trust Deed.

The proposed changes would:

change the Trust’s balance date and income year so future AGMs can be held in February or March, during Raumati
make transitional changes to some Trustee terms
clarify how casual Trustee vacancies are filled
update the Trust Deed to reflect changes to the Māori Fisheries Act 2004

Moving future AGMs to Raumati is intended to make it easier for more whānau to travel home and participate.

Voting on the proposed amendments

Resolutions 1 to 4 will be decided by postal and online voting. Voting closes at 12 noon on Friday, 11 September 2026.

Resolutions 5 and 6, confirming that the proposed amendments are for the collective benefit of Ngāti Apa ki te Rā Tō, will be decided in person at the Special General Meeting as part of the meeting agenda.

long_description:
Overview

Your perspective is not a problem to solve. It is material.

A poetry zine is a tiny act of self-publishing: a place for sharp thoughts, soft confessions, beautiful rage, private jokes, inconvenient truths, strange images and the parts of ourselves we are often taught to make smaller.

In this two-hour Guerrilla Poetry workshop, poet and collage artist Rowan Taigel will invite you to cut, write, tear, layer, rearrange, make space for contradiction - and make a handmade poetry zine that refuses to behave like a tidy little craft project.

A zine (pronounced ‘zeen’) is a small handmade place for the thoughts that do not fit neatly into the version of the world we have been handed: beautiful rage and ordinary tenderness; difficult questions and private jokes; grief and glamour; politics and pleasure; softness and refusal.

This is for people who are drawn to art, language, DIY culture and creative expression. For anyone who has ever been called too much, too intense, too sensitive, too political, too imaginative, or simply “extra” - but may need someone to hand them the scissors and say: start here.

Come and make a tiny publication with people who also see the cracks in the story and feel compelled to write in them. Something interesting is bound to happen.

No experience is needed. Bring your curiosity, your opinions, and any feelings that might benefit from becoming art.

Leave with your own handmade poetry zine: clever, strange, beautiful, defiant, or all four.

Part of Beautiful Words at Project 100. All materials provided.
